newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold to struggle on the upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold to struggle on the upside.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

Gold needs to break above resistance at $330.00 an ounce to extend the current run higher, but several traders remain wary over the market's potential to fall to recent lows amid a lack of strong consumer demand.
Silver is likely to find resistance above $4.30, while platinum will struggle to overcome $410.00, traders said on Monday.
GOLD - Despite investment fund buying in the U.S., gold was unlikely to surmount resistance above $330.00 an ounce, traders and analysts said.
"We are looking at a market that is on a bounce to nowhere," one trader commented.
The trader believed that gold would retreat towards $300.00 in the coming weeks amid a lack of upside confidence following its recent plunge to 12-year lows of around $313.60.
Referring to the August gold contract, Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said, "To confirm a return to the uptrend look to see resistance at $330.00 then $334.00 successfully negotiated.
"Until then we remain marginally in favour of further downside tests."
Some support was seen at $325.00, followed by $320.00.
At 0730 GMT spot gold was indicated at $327.80/$328.30, versus Friday's London close of $323.90/$324.40.
SILVER - Expected to find resistance above $4.30 an ounce and may pull back towards support at recent lows of $417.00/$418.00. Above $4.30, resistance is seen at $4.40.00
At 0730 GMT spot silver was indicated at $4.31/$4.33, against $4.29/$4.31.
PLATINUM - Seen struggling to overcome resistance at $410.00, with $420.00 seen as a stiff barrier on any thrust higher.
Support pegged at $394.00.
At 0730 GMT platinum was quoted at $410.00/$413.00 as it made an early probe above initial resistance. That compared with $406.00/$409.00 on Friday.
